title: Shielded rollout eval proxy for customer-isolated config changes
creator: Asha Kulkarni
description: Summary: Build a shielded evaluation proxy that sits in front of customer-serving rollout traffic to run customer-scoped, privacy-preserving evals when config or model variants change. The proxy must operate for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private/VPC customers with strict data isolation and optional zero-telemetry mode. Goals: (1) detect regressions tied to config/model changes before 100% rollouts, (2) provide encrypted local golden sets and deterministic checksums, (3) allow silent shadow runs with client-side redaction/hashing and customer opt-in for aggregated telemetry, (4) enable automated rollback triggers and audit trails for compliance. Success metrics: catch >=90% of high-severity regressions during canary windows, reduce customer-impacting rollbacks in prod by 40% over the next two quarters, and achieve <5ms median added latency for proxy/non-blocking shadow path.
implementation_notes: Architecture: proxy receives routed requests per rollout policy; for customers with shielded-eval enabled it mirrors requests to a local eval runner that holds encrypted golden sets. The runner executes evaluation harness (deterministic prompts + metrics) using a pinned model variant. Privacy: input payloads can be pre-processed at the client or edge with HMAC-anchored prompt hashes and selective redaction. Golden sets are stored encrypted with customer KMS keys (Dedicated/Private) or RW-managed envelope encryption for Hosted with configurable retention. Telemetry gating: only aggregate metrics (delta counts, histogram buckets) leave the customer boundary unless explicit consent is recorded. Rollout gating: the proxy emits a composite score to the rollout controller; if regressions exceed configured thresholds the controller will auto-pause or roll back the variant. Observability: per-tenant eval dashboards, signed audit entries for every run, and downloadable encrypted artifacts for customer audits.
engineering_risks:
- Ensuring deterministic eval runs across quantized/accelerated kernels.
- Preventing accidental exfiltration of PII when running shadow evaluations (mitigation: default redaction + hash anchors).
- Latency amplification for extremely short-SLO workloads; require non-blocking mirror path and adaptive sampling.
- Key management complexity for cross-cloud private deployments.
